Looking ahead, South Sudan’s operating environment and economic
prospects will continue to hinge on the sustained operation of oil
infrastructure, progress in the peace process and improvements in fiscal and
liquidity management.
Against this backdrop, the near‑term outlook is best characterised as fragile
but selectively opportunity‑driven. While headline growth may remain
positive if oil production is sustained, underlying vulnerabilities like inflation,
liquidity constraints and security risks are expected to persist.
Accordingly, the operating environment will continue to favour a measured
and risk‑reward balanced approach, with emphasis on:
• Controlled growth, aligned to core client needs and essential economic
activity
• Liquidity and balance‑sheet resilience, to withstand ongoing volatility
• Digital and cross‑border solutions, including enhancing ‘Thunes’
and supporting money movement and regional livelihoods in a
cash‑constrained economy
Overall, disciplined execution, strong governance and selective innovation are
expected to remain central to navigating South Sudan’s complex operating
environment as we navigate the regulatory directives particularly on
increased capital requirements.
